handoff.purpose: CLI entrypoint for daedalus.eval: tiered runs, baseline gate/update, and minting/confirming tasks.

symbols.name: _select
symbols.note: Filters all tasks by project label; raises SystemExit if no matches and project given.

symbols.name: _print_ascii
symbols.note: Prints text, falling back to ASCII-replace encoding on UnicodeEncodeError.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: Parses args and dispatches to mint, confirm, baseline, gate, or tier runs. Minting writes to mint store; updating baseline writes baseline.json.

claims.why: main() unconditionally calls run_tier1(tasks) at the end, with no flag guarding it.

claims.text: --arms adds the deterministic A/B/C retrieval comparison (also no LLM).
claims.why: run_arms(tasks) is called only when args.arms is set; the flag help says it is deterministic, and nothing in this chunk contradicts it.

claims.text: Tier 2 runs only with --tier2 AND a reachable provider; otherwise it is skipped with a clear message.
claims.why: This chunk only gates run_tier2 on args.tier2. Provider reachability and the clear message are inside run_tier2, not visible here.

claims.text: --gate is an ADVISORY local regression check against baseline.json
claims.why: main() calls harness.run_gate(tasks, baseline_path=args.baseline_path) when args.gate is set; the flag help calls it ADVISORY and the exit code is not wired to anything automatic.

claims.text: It is never wired into anything automatic; run it by hand before shipping a slice-heuristic change.
claims.why: This chunk only defines the CLI. Whether offload.py or other modules invoke main() with --gate cannot be determined from this file alone.

claims.text: --update-baseline is the only thing that writes baseline.json, and only when explicitly passed.
claims.why: This chunk confirms that --update-baseline calls harness.write_baseline, but it cannot prove that no other code writes baseline.json.

claims.text: --mint-commit/--confirm-mint are the ONLY entry points that persist a task to the mint store
claims.why: This chunk shows add_minted_task and confirm_minted_task are called from these flags, but cannot prove no other module writes to the mint store.

claims.text: every other flag above only READS it via harness.all_tasks()
claims.why: The read path is all_tasks() via _select, but this chunk cannot rule out other writes elsewhere in the codebase.

claims.text: This is the human-invoked half of the mint -> quarantine -> confirm -> primary flywheel -- there is no automatic caller (offload.py does not invoke this today; see mint.py's module docstring).
claims.why: No offload.py content is in this chunk; the claim about it cannot be checked here.

claims.text: Output is ASCII-only for a raw Windows console.
claims.why: _print_ascii catches UnicodeEncodeError and writes ASCII-replaced bytes to sys.stdout.buffer, used for gate and final render output.

claims.text: Tier 1 and --arms are deterministic (no LLM); Tier 2 is opt-in; --gate is an advisory local regression check.
claims.why: The code gates arms and tier2 behind flags; nothing in this chunk invokes an LLM for tier1 or arms.

claims.text: Exits non-zero on a regression; never blocks anything automatic.
claims.why: main returns 0 if gate['passed'] else 1, and there is no automatic invocation here.

claims.text: EXPLICIT ONLY: overwrite baseline.json with current recall. Never happens automatically.
claims.why: write_baseline is called only when args.update_baseline is set; no other branch in this chunk writes baseline.json.

claims.text: EXPLICIT ONLY: mint a quarantined, independent_diff task from git commit SHA in --repo ... and persist it to the mint store so it joins every subsequent run via all_tasks().
claims.why: mint_from_commit is called only when args.mint_commit is set, and add_minted_task persists it; the task will be read by all_tasks later.

claims.text: EXPLICIT ONLY: record one independent confirmation for a quarantined minted task, promoting it to primary at daedalus.eval.mint.MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD.
claims.why: The promotion logic and threshold are in mint.py, not this chunk; confirm_minted_task is called here but its internal behavior is not visible.

claims.text: repo root for --mint-commit (default: this agent_env checkout).
claims.why: repo = args.repo or AGENT_ENV_ROOT, with AGENT_ENV_ROOT imported from .tasks.

claims.text: override the mint store path (default: daedalus/eval/minted_tasks.json).
claims.why: args.mint_store_path is passed to add_minted_task and confirm_minted_task; the default is stated in the help and the module constant is in mint.py.

observations.what: The docstring claims --mint-commit/--confirm-mint are the ONLY entry points persisting to the mint store, but this chunk cannot verify that; other modules may write.
When --gate is used, tier1/arms/tier2 are not run at all; the gate path returns early. This is consistent with the advisory semantics but means --gate and --tier2 are mutually exclusive in effect.
If --update-baseline and --gate are both passed, --update-baseline wins because it is checked first; the gate is ignored.

_print_ascii catches UnicodeEncodeError on print, but if the text already contains characters that fail ascii encoding, the fallback writes to sys.stdout.buffer without flushing; a subsequent normal print may interleave incorrectly.

risks: docstring lines 12-13 | medium | Claim that only --mint-commit/--confirm-mint persist to mint store is unverifiable here; other modules might write. | Check mint.py and other callers of add_minted_task/confirm_minted_task.
main() lines 92-95 | low | --gate short-circuits before tier1/arms/tier2; users expecting both may be surprised. | Confirm documentation or intended behavior.
main() lines 86-95 | low | --update-baseline takes precedence over --gate; if both passed, gate is silently skipped. | Add validation or document precedence.
_print_ascii lines 29-33 | low | Fallback write to sys.stdout.buffer may not flush, risking interleaved output. | Verify with a test that triggers UnicodeEncodeError.
